projects.name: Track
projects.tagline: A calm, ad-free tracker for Indian trains and flights that also keeps your trips and tells you where to stand on the platform.
evidence: Searches 8,677 stations and 4,008 airports on the device, with no ads, sign-ups, cookies or analytics.
Shows the traveller's own stop as the hero of a train's status, and projects times for later stops from the latest actual delay, marked with a tilde and a range.
My journeys saves trips, passengers and PNRs on the device only; a PNR fills in a trip through the Worker, which does not log it.
Coach and berth guides cross-check three public sources and say how many place a coach, instead of guessing; a coach finder gives walking directions along the platform.
One Cloudflare Worker with nine API routes fronts more than ten public sources, and shares a free-tier flight quota across visitors through caches and a daily budget.
73 offline tests pass against recorded real responses; plain JavaScript modules with no build step, installable with Add to Home Screen.

projects.name: Chalk
projects.tagline: Snooker and 8-ball pool scored and explained, for people who have never played.
evidence: A phone-first scoreboard and rules coach for snooker and 8-ball pool: the player taps what happened on the table and the app keeps the score, the turn and what is on next.
A "What happened?" screen asks what the white hit and what went in, then explains the foul ruling and the penalty points in plain words.
Pool follows the WPA Rules of Play effective 15 September 2025; 128 quick answers (76 snooker, 52 pool) cover common "what if" questions.

Two phones can score one game through a link or QR code; the Cloudflare Worker re-checks every move with the same rules engine as the page and refuses out-of-turn moves, and moves queue on the phone when signal drops.
81 unit tests pass across both rules engines, match flow and the Worker, with a browser test file and a GitHub Actions workflow.
No ads, no sign-ups, no build step and no runtime dependencies; a service worker makes it installable.

projects.name: Shelfie
projects.tagline: A reading tracker you drive with your thumbs: flick, drag, drop, level up.
evidence: Books are arcade passes you flick through, drag up to turn pages and drop onto four shelf zones; every move is a spring that keeps the finger's speed.
Progress is a game: XP, 9 levels from Fresh Spine to Literary Final Boss, streaks, goals and 20 badges that peel off as die-cut stickers.
All 30 sounds are synthesised in the browser with Web Audio; the repo has no audio files.
Motion controls are tuned on two real iPhone recordings that are committed as fixtures and replayed by the tests.
Books live on the device; an optional account syncs an end-to-end encrypted copy (AES-256-GCM, key derived with PBKDF2) that the Cloudflare Worker and D1 database cannot read.
105 unit tests and 37 browser tests run in CI on every push; no ads, cookies or analytics, and no build step.

projects.name: Decoding Credit Cards
projects.tagline: 22 interactive chapters on how credit cards actually work, for India.
evidence: The guide has 22 chapter pages, each built around one interaction, from a 5-step transaction lifecycle to a live minimum-payment debt simulator.
The minimum-payment chapter models a Rs 50,000 balance at 36% APR and shows that paying only the minimum costs 2.75 times the original amount.
Three chapters cover fraud and disputes, including 6 fraud scenarios across phishing, skimming, vishing and dynamic currency conversion.
It ends with a 10-question test that draws on the earlier chapters, and a diploma.
Plain HTML, CSS and JavaScript with zero JavaScript dependencies and no build step; no analytics, login, affiliate links or card recommendations, and the only third-party request is Google Fonts.
The page's own time estimates add up to 141 minutes across the 22 chapters.

projects.name: Zero to a Hundred
projects.tagline: An open, vendor-neutral curriculum for learning AI in 22 phases, from ML basics to the open-weights-or-API decision.
evidence: The path has 22 phases in two parts: 14 on understanding and building with AI, and 8 on running, serving, evaluating and fine-tuning open models.
It carries 175 concepts and 129 resource cards, 126 of them tagged free and 3 tagged paid.
Every phase opens with a "When this is done" outcome and closes with a "Skip this" note on what not to spend time on.
Part two follows one running project through every phase and ends in a decision memo with an 8-dimension scorecard comparing open weights with an API.
A searchable dictionary covers 585 AI terms in 17 categories.
The whole site is one HTML file of about 359 KB, with no build step or framework.

projects.name: Jira 2.0
projects.tagline: A teardown and clickable prototype of an AI layer on Jira, where every suggestion shows its reasoning.
evidence: A Today/2.0 toggle runs the same sample dataset through a replica of current Jira and through the new AI-native layer.
The AI answers are scripted samples: there are no network calls, and natural-language questions are matched to 5 canned query results.
The home screen changes by persona, with three separate home views for Product Manager, Engineer and Engineering Manager.
Clicking an AI suggestion opens a drawer with signals used, reasoning and a confidence bar, plus the cost of being wrong where a record defines it.
Ticket creation drafts from free text, flags ambiguous fields as low confidence and asks the user to confirm before anything is filed.
Dashboard questions turn into visible JQL and switch between table, bar and line views; a companion product teardown deck is linked.

projects.name: GRID
projects.tagline: An editorial reference for Formula 1's 2026 reset, with live timing from OpenF1.
evidence: Five pages cover a primer, 11 teams and 22 drivers, a 22-race calendar with a drawn silhouette per circuit, the car, live timing and a learn section.
The live page requests drivers, positions, laps, weather and race control in parallel, so one failed feed does not blank the others.
API calls are queued with a 600 ms gap, time out after 10 seconds and are cached in localStorage with a stale fallback.
Championship standings are recomputed in the browser from completed Race and Sprint results and cached for 12 hours, with a static snapshot as fallback.
A 60-lap strategy simulator charges 22 seconds per stop, adds a tyre wear penalty and enforces the two-compound rule; a pit-stop game adds 0.5 seconds per wrong wheel.
About 251 KiB uncompressed and about 64 KB gzipped, with no framework or build step.

projects.name: The Cookbook
projects.tagline: 216 dishes and drinks that start from context, not chapters.
evidence: Starts from six context entry points (20 minutes, I have chicken, zero cleanup, someone's coming over, post-workout, behind the bar) instead of chapters.
A fridge matcher ranks dishes by weighted set overlap with the ingredients you have, counting the main protein double.
A 14-day planner totals macros and builds a combined grocery list; 7 host menus come with runsheets.
Cook mode is a full-screen step player with timers and a screen wake lock; the 80 drinks (27 cafe, 53 bar) get a pour mode.
Data model: 216 cards, 233 ingredients with macros per 100 g, 421 aliases and 1,009 relationship links; every card's macros are computed from the ingredient database.
A Python validator checks references, tags, relationships and macros, and is run before each deploy.

projects.name: Map Poster Studio
projects.tagline: Turn any place or one of 96 race circuits into a print-ready poster, wallpaper or 3D skyline, in the browser.
projects.based_on: A fork of City Roads by Andrei Kashcha (anvaka/city-roads)
evidence: Builds on Andrei Kashcha's open-source City Roads and extends it with a poster studio, 96 pre-extracted race circuits and a Skyline perspective view.
The studio offers 24 looks, layers, solid and gradient paints, neon, emboss and blur effects, street selection, and export to PNG, JPEG, WebP, AVIF or SVG at 150, 300 or 600 dpi.
Map data now loads from OpenFreeMap vector tiles in a web worker, with VersaTiles and Overpass as fallbacks.
Removed the upstream analytics and a third-party mug shop, added a Content-Security-Policy, and cut dependency audit findings from 10 to 0.
A GitHub Actions workflow lints, builds and deploys to GitHub Pages on each push; about 11,000 lines were added across about 216 files compared with upstream. There are no automated tests.
